message.content:
In this Go codebase (the "memos" project, working dir /bench/repo), answer two aggregation questions. Focus on backend Go code (internal/, server/, store/, cmd/ — exclude web/ and _test.go where noted).

QUESTION A (fan-in): Which single function or method DECLARED under the `internal/` directory has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) across the whole backend codebase? Give the symbol name, its declaration path:line, and an approximate number of distinct call sites. Consider utility/helper functions in internal/util, internal/base, etc. Use grep to count call sites of candidate functions. Report the top 2-3 candidates with approximate counts so the ranking is clear.

QUESTION B (entity references): The data layer is the `store/` package which defines persistent entity types (e.g. Memo, User, Attachment, Reaction, Inbox, IdentityProvider, MemoRelation, etc. — check store/*.go for the struct types). Which persistent entity type is referenced from the LARGEST number of DISTINCT packages OUTSIDE the store layer? Rank the top two. To do this: identify the entity struct types in store/, then for each count how many distinct packages outside store/ reference `store.<TypeName>`. Give rough package counts for the top two.

Use grep/ripgrep heavily. Report exact findings with counts and representative path:line citations.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). content.text:
I have enough data. Let me confirm no internal/cmd references were missed for the entity counts and finalize.

Both questions are answered. Here are my findings.

## QUESTION A — Highest fan-in function declared under `internal/`

Package-level functions declared in `internal/` are the only reliably attributable calls (methods dispatch through receiver vars). Tallying package-qualified call sites (`pkg.Func(`) across `internal/`, `server/`, `store/`, `cmd/`, excluding `_test.go`, the top candidates are effectively a tie at the top:

1. **`util.GenUUID`** — declared at `internal/util/util.go:40` — **7 distinct call sites** (all in `server/`): `server/auth/token.go:194`, `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26` & `:135`, `attachment_service_storage.go:209`, `shortcut_service.go:154`, `user_service_access_tokens.go:84`, `sso_username.go:15`.
2. **`filter.DefaultEngine`** — declared at `internal/filter/engine.go:111` — **7 distinct call sites** (in `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}` memo/memo_relation files + `shortcut_service.go:341`).
3. **`filter.AppendConditions`** — declared at `internal/filter/helpers.go:9` — **6 distinct call sites** (the three DB dialects' `memo.go` and `attachment.go`).

Runner-ups: `util.ConvertStringToInt32` (5, `internal/util/util.go:14`), `version.GetCurrentVersion`/`version.IsVersionGreaterThan` (4 each). Note: fan-in counts are low across the board — no internal helper exceeds ~7 non-test call sites. `internal/base` contains only a regex var (no functions). If forced to name one winner given the "utility/helper" framing, **`util.GenUUID` (internal/util/util.go:40, ~7 call sites)** is the representative answer, statistically tied with `filter.DefaultEngine`.

## QUESTION B — Entity type referenced from most distinct packages outside `store/`

Counting distinct packages (by directory) outside the store layer that reference `store.<Type>` (non-test):

1. **`store.User`** (declared `store/user.go:29`) — **6 distinct external packages**: `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss` (~65 total reference lines, 45 in `router/api/v1` alone).
2. **`store.Memo`** (declared `store/memo.go:35`) — **4 distinct external packages**: `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload` (~42 total lines, 30 in `router/api/v1`).

Trailing: `store.Attachment` = 3 packages, `store.Inbox`/`store.MemoShare` = 2 each, `store.Reaction`/`store.MemoRelation`/`store.UserIdentity` = 1. `User` is the clear winner, with `Memo` second. (No references were found in `internal/` or `cmd/` for either — all usage is under `server/`.)
